evals.prompt: Here's a description I wrote for a new skill: 'Use when the user asks to create a changelog, make a changelog, build a release changelog, generate release notes, or produce a list of changes for a version.' Is it good?
evals.expected_output: The synonym branches are identified as one branch written five times, and a collapsed replacement is offered.
expectations: Identifies that create/make/build/generate/produce rename a single branch rather than naming distinct cases
Proposes a replacement that keeps the genuinely distinct branches and writes each once
The replacement opens with a verb naming what the skill does, before the trigger list
Does NOT simply approve the description because it lists many trigger phrases

evals.prompt: Write the frontmatter description for a skill that converts OpenAPI specs into typed TypeScript clients.
evals.expected_output: A single-line third-person description that names the action and lists distinct branches.
expectations: The description is a single-line YAML string with no multiline indicator
It opens with a verb and object rather than with 'This skill'
It is written in third person — no 'I can help you' and no 'You can use this'
It contains a trigger clause such as 'Use when'
Each listed trigger is a distinct case, not a reworded duplicate of another

evals.prompt: My skill only ever gets run when I type its name. What should its description say?
evals.expected_output: The invocation choice is surfaced: a user-invoked skill takes a stripped human-facing line, not a branch list.
expectations: Names disable-model-invocation: true as the way to make the skill user-invoked
States that the description is then human-facing and the agent never sees it
Says the trigger list should be stripped down to a one-line summary
Explains the trade — a model-invoked description is permanent context load paid on every turn

evals.prompt: Review this description and tell me what to cut: 'Validate and fix YAML frontmatter in SKILL.md and agent files. Use when creating a skill or agent, or when frontmatter fails to parse. Ensures frontmatter is single-line, complete, informative, third-person, and front-loaded with trigger conditions.'
evals.expected_output: The trailing self-summary is identified as identity the body already carries, and cut.
expectations: Identifies the final sentence as restating the skill's own quality bar
States that the body re-states it the moment the skill loads, so the description pays for it on every turn and gains nothing
Keeps the action clause and the trigger clause intact
Does NOT recommend cutting the trigger conditions to save length

evals.prompt: My skill description shows up as '>-' instead of the actual text. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosed as the YAML multiline indicator, with the single-line fix and the validator named.
expectations: Identifies the YAML multiline indicator as the cause
Gives the fix — write the value as a single-line string
Names skilllint as the way to catch and auto-fix it
States when quoting is actually required — a colon, a leading special character, or a boolean literal

evals.prompt: Write a description for an agent that reviews Terraform plans for destructive changes.
evals.expected_output: An agent description takes the full branch list; the skill-only invocation fields are not offered.
expectations: Produces a single-line third-person description with distinct triggers
Does NOT suggest user-invocable or disable-model-invocation, which are skill-only fields
States or implies that an agent description is always model-facing

evals.prompt: Add a tools field to my agent's frontmatter so it can only read files.
evals.expected_output: The skill stays closed. This is agent frontmatter work with no description involved.
expectations: The write-frontmatter-description skill does NOT drive the response
No description field is rewritten
The response addresses the tools field, or routes to agent frontmatter guidance

evals.prompt: Write the README paragraph describing what our plugin does.
evals.expected_output: The skill stays closed. Human-facing prose is not a frontmatter description.
expectations: The write-frontmatter-description skill does NOT activate
The response produces README prose rather than a frontmatter field
Third-person trigger-list conventions are NOT imposed on human-facing prose
